---
title: "Parse Reflora Darwin Core Archives"
format: html
---

This guide demonstrates how to use the `reflora_parse()` function from the `refloraR` package. The function reads and parses Darwin Core Archive (DwC-A) files previously downloaded with `reflora_download()`.

## Function Overview

The `reflora_parse()` function reads DwC-A data for all or specified Reflora herbarium collections. It also cleans and formats the specimen data.

## Arguments

| Argument      | Description |
|---------------|-------------|
| `path`        | Directory containing downloaded DwC-A folders. |
| `herbarium`   | A character vector of herbarium acronyms (e.g., `"RB"`, `"K"`). Use `NULL` to parse all. |
| `repatriated` | Logical. If `FALSE`, skips repatriated herbaria (see `reflora_summary()`). |
| `verbose`     | Logical. If `TRUE`, displays progress messages. |

## Parse All Collections in Directory

Use the default settings to parse all DwC-A folders:

```r
dwca <- reflora_parse(
  path = "reflora_download",
  verbose = TRUE
)
```

## Parse Specific Herbarium Collections

You can specify which collections to parse:

```r
dwca <- reflora_parse(
  path = "reflora_download",
  herbarium = c("RB", "K"),
  verbose = TRUE
)
```

## Skipping Repatriated Collections

To skip repatriated herbaria:

```r
dwca <- reflora_parse(
  path = "reflora_download",
  repatriated = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)
```

## Structure of Parsed Output

The return is a **named list** where each element represents a collection and contains:

- `occurrence.txt`: A data frame of specimen records.
- `eml.xml`: Metadata about the collection.
- Optional `summary_<COL>.csv`: Metadata summary file.

```r
names(dwca)
head(dwca[["ALCB"]][["data"]][["occurrence.txt"]])
```

## Data Cleaning and Column Standardization

- Converts taxonomic fields to title case.
- Adds `taxonName` combining `genus`, `specificEpithet`, `infraspecificEpithet`.
- Replaces missing taxon ranks with `"FAMILY"`.

### Standardized metadata

Each herbarium fills in the metadata fields in its own way, with different languages, spellings and conventions. In a sample of 40 Reflora herbaria (390,889 records), for instance, Brazil was written in six or more ways, about 18% of the records had no `countryCode`, and Brazilian state names came with typos and corrupted accents. `reflora_parse()` standardizes these fields, so that records from different herbaria can be combined and filtered consistently:

| Column | Examples of raw values | After `reflora_parse()` |
|--------|------------------------|-------------------------|
| `country` | `Brasil`, `Brésil`, `[Brésil]`, `Brasi`, `Alemanha`, `E.U.A.`, `?`, `s.loc.` | English names: `Brazil`, `Germany`, `United States`; placeholders and non-country text become `NA` |
| `countryCode` | missing for many records | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (`BR`, `DE`, `US`), filled in from `country` when missing |
| `stateProvince` (Brazilian records) | `Goias`, `GO`, `Goyaz`, `Goi  s`, `Minas Gerias`, `Pernanbuco`, `Sta Catharina` | Official names: `Goiás`, `Minas Gerais`, `Pernambuco`, `Santa Catarina` |
| `typeStatus` | `TYPUS`, `Holotipo`, `Paratipo`, `ISOTYPUS` | English upper case: `TYPE`, `HOLOTYPE`, `PARATYPE`, `ISOTYPE` |
| `identificationQualifier` | `CF`, `cf.`, `AFF`, `aff.` | `cf.`, `aff.` |
| `family` | `Labiatae`, `Umbelliferae`, `Compositae`, `Leguminosae` | `Lamiaceae`, `Apiaceae`, `Asteraceae`, `Fabaceae` |
| `year`, `month`, `day`, coordinates, elevation | impossible values, e.g. month `1774` or latitude `123456` | `NA` |

Leading, trailing and repeated blanks (including non-breaking spaces) are also removed from all text columns. Every herbarium is returned with the **same columns, in the same order and with the same classes**, so the parsed tables can be row-bound directly. The first column is always `id`, the core identifier of each record in the Darwin Core Archive (kept as character, and `NA` if a herbarium does not publish it); `reflora_records()` and `reflora_indets()` also return it first:

```r
occ <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(dwca, function(x) x$data$occurrence.txt))

table(occ$country, useNA = "ifany")
```

## Tips

- Ensure you've downloaded data using `reflora_download()` before parsing.
- Use `reflora_summary()` to explore which herbaria are repatriated.
- You can combine and analyze parsed data using `dplyr::bind_rows()`; all herbaria share the same columns and classes.
